question: Order ORD-023 was split into two shipments. Give me the status of each and explain why it was split.
agent_answer:
Here's the full picture for ORD-023 (OMS: urgent order for Mandarin Oriental, shipped 2026-02-12):

## Shipment Status

| Shipment | Carrier | Type | Products | Status | ETA |
|----------|---------|------|----------|--------|-----|
| SHP-017 | SCG Cold Chain (CAR-002) | Refrigerated | PROD-001 — Nam Doc Mai Mango Box 5kg (×10) | In transit | 2026-02-13 |
| SHP-018 | Kerry Express (CAR-001) | Ground | PROD-006 — Dried Mango Slices 500g (×60) | In transit | 2026-02-14 |

## Why It Was Split

The two order lines have incompatible storage requirements (WMS):

- **PROD-001** — fresh mangoes, `storage_type: refrigerated`, 7-day shelf life → **must** travel in a cold chain truck (SHP-017 via SCG Cold Chain ✓)
- **PROD-006** — dried mango slices, `storage_type: ambient`, 180-day shelf life → standard ground delivery is fine (SHP-018 via Kerry Express ✓)

This is the correct approach. Putting fresh mangoes on a ground carrier would violate the cold chain rule and risk spoilage. The split also has a cost benefit: ambient freight via Kerry Express (15 THB/kg) is cheaper than cold chain (25 THB/kg), so only the perishable line pays the premium rate.

Both shipments are in transit and on track to arrive before the required date of 2026-02-15.
